intelligence.human_view: The walk began with a tap that did nothing (SN-3001, 18:56Z): he tapped the My World chip, the picker popped up, he picked his world — "and then I put my world and then nothing happened." A picker that opens and lets you choose and then does nothing with the choice is a dead end wearing a menu's clothes; the rule is absolute — the tap IS the switch. One minute later the charge (SN-3002, 18:57Z): "you got rid of what was good, which you do that often" — the five-icon bottom bar was good and got replaced by a nine-icon row plus a MAIL/ACTIVITY/SPACES row that wasn't good. The fix is restoration, harvested byte for byte from the build that had it right; the nine go in the sidebars in logical order. The same minute, the presentation rule (SN-3003): one icon that lights up, never an icon beside its own light — the composer controls' little lights become the icons themselves. Then the question about the extra + (SN-3004, 18:58Z): two plus buttons, two jobs — LEFT + CREATE, RIGHT + CONNECT — and the mobile fit decides: if it fits perfectly on one line at phone width, keep it; if it wraps, the right + moves to the corner. The measurement said it fits — all six on one line, nothing cut off. Then the modal (SN-3005, 18:59Z): "That looks like shit. You need to make not flat buttons all depth and nice and primo and then actually when you do that it should actually create the feed and show you the feed" — flat buttons and a dead end are one failure, not two. Then the button (SN-3006, 19:02Z): "Captain's eye test world" cuts off its own text — and the cause is named in the same breath: eye checks left a test world behind. Then the eye itself (SN-3008, 19:03Z): the ⓘ is a blob, "you can barely see it's an I" — and the fix is not a better drawing but the pricing eye, harvested verbatim, white and pearl with a purple edge light. Then the depth (SN-3009, 19:07Z): clone it once, put the clone behind, move it just a tad — that is how a flat thing becomes a real object. And between them the operating shape (SN-3007, 19:14Z) and the queued feature (SN-3010, 19:07Z): the team on fire 24-7, finished pieces every few minutes, and leaderboards so citizens see where they score in any area.
intelligence.simple_view: Imagine a magic TV remote. You press the button for cartoons — and NOTHING happens! That is not a magic remote. It is a broken one! When you press cartoons, the TV must switch to cartoons RIGHT AWAY. That is what the button is FOR! And imagine you built a beautiful tower out of blocks. Someone knocks it down and builds a wobbly one. You do not keep the wobbly one. You put YOUR tower back, block by block, just like before! And your favourite shiny star sticker? You use it again and again, everywhere. You do not draw a new different star every time! One star. One button. One job. Done!
intelligence.grandma_view: It's like this, love — imagine you press the button that says "garden," dear, and nothing happens at all! That's not a button, love — that's a picture of a button. A real button does its job the moment you press it. And imagine you made a lovely dinner, dear, and someone takes it away and serves something that isn't nearly as nice. Oh, love — you put the lovely dinner back on the table, just the way it was! And if you've got a beautiful button in your sewing box, dear, you use the beautiful one you already have — you don't make a new one every time! One good thing, used everywhere, love. That's the sensible way.
intelligence.naya_view: Every control must do its job. A picker that switches nothing is a dead end; a create that creates nothing goes nowhere; a button that cuts off its text is not a button. When his eye says something was better before, I restore the good version verbatim — I do not improve on it, redesign it, or put something else in. One icon that lights up, never an icon beside its own light. One eye, not a new eye per page — the pricing eye, harvested verbatim and double-layered for depth. And the team runs on fire 24-7, because the finish is the trigger, not the clock.
